summary: Provision dedicated perf-lab capacity for FP8/INT8 benchmark sprint (H200 + L40S) and reduce node contention/isolation issues
description:
Requesting dedicated, isolated perf-lab capacity for the FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint to avoid noisy-neighbor effects and reduce run-to-run variance.

Background
- We are seeing high variance + intermittent stalls in end-to-end benchmark runs (TTFT/TPOT + throughput) that correlate with node contention and background activity.
- Sprint requires defensible baseline + delta reporting across A100/H100/H200/L40S; H200 and L40S coverage is currently the bottleneck.

Ask (capacity)
1) H200: Provision dedicated nodes in perf-lab (target: 2 nodes minimum; 4 nodes preferred) for nightly canary + ad-hoc matrix runs.
2) L40S: Provision dedicated nodes (target: 2 nodes) with stable driver/CUDA and consistent clocks.
3) Reservation model: Ability to reserve a node pool for benchmark-lab jobs during agreed windows (e.g., 10am–6pm PT) to avoid random preemption/competition.

Ask (isolation / stability)
- Create a dedicated node pool (or equivalent) with:
  - Taints/labels so only benchmark-lab workloads schedule there.
  - No opportunistic/background jobs (indexers, unrelated CI runners, etc.) on these nodes.
  - Disable GPU sharing/MIG unless explicitly required; prefer full-GPU allocation for consistent perf.
  - Fixed/pinned GPU clocks where allowed (or document why not feasible); ensure persistence mode.
  - Consistent container base image + driver/CUDA versions per the sprint environment pinning.

Acceptance criteria
- Benchmark-lab jobs scheduled on the dedicated pool show:
  - Reduced variance: <= 3% run-to-run variability on tokens/sec for fixed microbench shapes and standard end-to-end scenario (same model/workload parameters).
  - No unexplained >10% perf drops attributable to host/node contention.
  - Clear labeling in metrics/logs so we can separate runs executed on the dedicated pool.
- H200 and L40S nodes are accessible to benchmark-lab service account(s) and documented in the runbook.

Dependencies / references
- ENG-24813 (Expand GPU coverage to H200 + L40S)
- ENG-24812 (Pin reproducible perf-lab environment)
- #eng-sre thread on contention + scheduling isolation (see internal Slack ref in comments)

Notes
- This is internal-only perf infrastructure; not customer-facing. However, this is gating release decisions for quantized paths, so timeline is tight (need capacity by mid-sprint).
